title: Learning Morse code as a mixtape: letters by rhythm
summary: Learn Morse the way you learn songs: by rhythm and sound, in tracks, not by memorizing a chart of dots and dashes.

blocks.title: Morse is music before it is spelling
blocks.body: People fail Morse by counting dots. People learn Morse by hearing rhythms - each letter is a little riff. This mixtape teaches the alphabet in tracks, each track a set of letters whose rhythms contrast enough to tell apart.

blocks.heading: How to listen to a track
items: Say each letter's pattern out loud as a rhythm: dit for a dot, dah for a dash.
Listen for the shape, never the count - di-DAH is A the way a hook is a chorus.
Run the track until you can hear the letter before your brain finishes the sound.
Only then move to the next track. Speed comes free; counting is what costs.

blocks.heading: Track one - the heartbeat letters
blocks.caption: Eight letters cover half of ordinary English. This track alone can already spell TEA, TIME, NAME.

blocks.heading: Track two - the swing letters
blocks.caption: Now you can spell WORK, DARK, GUIDE, and the most important word in radio: CW.

blocks.heading: Track three - the B-sides
blocks.caption: The deep cuts. Notice C has its own bounce - dah-di-DAH-dit sounds like a horse at a gallop.

blocks.heading: Why the track order works
blocks.body: Each track adds letters whose rhythms are maximally different from what you already know, so confusion has nowhere to hide. The classic mistake is learning the alphabet in order - A, B, C, D - which teaches you the sequence of the alphabet, not the sound of the letters. In a real conversation nobody sends you the alphabet.

items.label: Five minutes: hear a letter, name it before the rhythm ends
items.detail: Any Morse practice app on random letters, one track at a time.

items.label: Five minutes: tap or hum words from your day
items.detail: COFFEE is dah-di-DAH-dit, dah-dah-dah, di-di-DAH-dit, di-di-DAH-dit, dit, dit. Now breakfast is practice.

items.label: Never translate through dots and dashes on paper
items.detail: Paper Morse trains reading, not hearing. The skill is sound to letter, direct.

blocks.heading: Check the rhythm
blocks.prompt: You hear di-di-dit. Which letter is it?
blocks.explanation: di-di-dit is three short beats: S. I is two (di-dit), and H is four (di-di-di-dit). The rhythm is the letter - no counting required once the track is burned in.
